tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.
- Prefer the Edit tool for modifying existing files — it only sends the diff. Only use this tool to create new files or for complete rewrites.
- NEVER create documentation files (*.md) or README files unless explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

schema_version: 1

project_stack:
  frontend:
    framework: Next.js
    routing: App Router
    ui_library: React
    language: TypeScript

  styling:
    preferred: Tailwind CSS
    alternative:
      name: Bootstrap
      use_when: "Continuity with the existing Bootstrap interface is required."

  backend:
    framework: Hono
    language: TypeScript
    role: HTTP API

  database:
    engine: PostgreSQL
    orm: Prisma
    schema_strategy:
      - control
      - project

  background_jobs:
    status: undecided
    options:
      - pg-boss
      - BullMQ

  validation:
    library: Zod

  testing:
    unit_and_integration: Vitest
    end_to_end: Playwright

  package_management:
    manager: pnpm
    workspace_strategy: pnpm workspaces

  runtime:
    local: Docker Compose
    development: Docker Compose
    test: Docker Compose

import { Navigate, Route, Routes } from 'react-router-dom'
import AppLayout from './layouts/AppLayout'
import DataExtraction from './pages/DataExtraction'
import Dashboard from './pages/Dashboard'
import Login from './pages/Login'
import Projects from './pages/Projects'
import QualityAssessment from './pages/QualityAssessment'
import QualityAssessmentDetail from './pages/QualityAssessmentDetail'
import Reports from './pages/Reports'
import Screening from './pages/Screening'
import ScreeningDetail from './pages/ScreeningDetail'

function App() {
  return (
    <Routes>
      <Route path="/" element={<Navigate to="/login" replace />} />
      <Route path="/login" element={<Login />} />
      <Route path="/projects" element={<Projects />} />
      <Route element={<AppLayout />}>
        <Route path="/dashboard" element={<Dashboard />} />
        <Route path="/screening" element={<Screening />} />
        <Route path="/screening/:paperId" element={<ScreeningDetail />} />
        <Route path="/quality-assessment" element={<QualityAssessment />} />
        <Route path="/quality-assessment/:paperId" element={<QualityAssessmentDetail />} />
        <Route path="/data-extraction" element={<DataExtraction />} />
        <Route path="/reports" element={<Reports />} />
      </Route>
    </Routes>
  )
}

export default App

# @relis/config

Single, typed, Zod-validated environment configuration contract shared by
`apps/web`, `apps/api`, `apps/worker`, migration tooling, and deployment
scripts. Each consumer imports only the loader for its own process, so it
never requires or receives configuration it doesn't need.

## Variables

| Variable | Category | Secret | Required by | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_ENV` | `core` | no | api, worker, web (server) | one of `development`, `test`, `production`; defaults to `development` |
| `PORT` | `network` | no | api (default `3001`), web server (default `3000`) | digits only, coerced to an integer in `1..65535` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `database` | **yes** | api, worker, migration | non-empty string matching `postgres(ql)://...` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `web-public` | no | web (browser) | absolute URL; inlined into the client bundle by Next.js at build time |

Every variable is declared once in `src/variables.ts`, including its
category and secrecy flag; process schemas in `src/processes/*.ts` compose
the subset each process actually needs.

## Process-specific contracts

| Process | Schema | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api` | `apiSchema` (`src/processes/api.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT` + `DATABASE_URL`. |
| `worker` | `workerSchema` (`src/processes/worker.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `DATABASE_URL`. No `PORT` — the worker has no HTTP surface. No queue/broker variable yet: `background_jobs` is still `undecided` (pg-boss vs. BullMQ) in `stack.yml`. |
| `web` (browser) | `webPublicSchema` (`src/processes/web.ts`) | Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`. Never includes `DATABASE_URL` or any other secret. Import via `@relis/config/web-public`, not `@relis/config`. |
| `web` (server) | `webServerSchema` | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT`. Still no secrets — the Next.js server in this repository does not talk to the database directly. |
| `migration` | `migrationSchema` (`src/processes/migration.ts`) | `DATABASE_URL` only. Not yet called from a real migration script — see the repository-level implementation report; no `packages/database` Prisma schema exists yet. |

## Usage

```ts
// apps/api/src/main.ts

# Shared environment configuration contract — see packages/config/README.md
# for the full per-process breakdown, validation rules, and error codes.
#
# Copy the variables a given process needs into its own .env (or your
# process manager / deployment secrets store). Never commit a real .env.

# --- web-public (apps/web browser bundle) -------------------------------
# Inlined into the client bundle at build time. Must never carry a secret.
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3001

# relis

pnpm workspace monorepo for the ReLiS application, following
[`../rules and context/project-structure.md`](../rules%20and%20context/project-structure.md)
and [`../rules and context/stack.yml`](../rules%20and%20context/stack.yml).

This is a minimal foundation created to support runtime configuration
validation (see `packages/config`). It intentionally does not yet include
a database schema, job queue, storage, auth, or CI/CD pipeline — those are
separate backlog items and out of scope here.

## Layout

```
relis/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ web/     Next.js App Router frontend. Shared layout + home page only,
│  │           adapted from v1/. See apps/web/src/shared/lib/mock-dashboard-data.ts
│  │           for the placeholder data it renders.
│  ├─ api/     Hono API. Entry point + health/readiness routes only — no
│  │           business modules yet.
│  └─ worker/  Minimal worker process shell — no job/queue processing yet.
├─ packages/
│  └─ config/  Shared, Zod-validated environment configuration contract
│              used by web, api, worker, and (once they exist) migration
│              and deployment tooling. See packages/config/README.md.
├─ .env.example
├─ pnpm-workspace.yaml
└─ tsconfig.base.json
```

## Scripts (run from `relis/`)

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck   # tsc --noEmit in every package/app
pnpm test        # vitest run in every package/app
pnpm build       # build every package/app
pnpm dev         # run web/api/worker dev servers in parallel
pnpm check:env -- <process>   # validate one process's env without starting it
```

Or scope any of the above to one project: `pnpm --filter @relis/api run test`.

## Environment configuration

Every process validates its own required environment variables before doing
any operational work (accepting HTTP traffic, processing jobs, or running
migrations), through the shared contract in `packages/config`. See:

- `packages/config/README.md` — variables, categories, per-process
  requirements, error codes.
- `.env.example` — safe example values (no real credentials).

## Known gaps

- **Migration tooling**: no `packages/database` Prisma schema exists yet,
  so `loadMigrationConfig()` (in `packages/config`) is defined but not
  called from any actual migration script.
- **Deployment**: no CI/CD pipeline or Docker Compose exists yet. A future
  pipeline can call `pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- <process>`
  once one is built.
- **apps/web**: only the shared layout and home/dashboard page were ported
  from `v1/`; all other v1 pages (login, screening, quality assessment,
  data extraction, reports) were intentionally not migrated. The home page
  renders mock data (`mock-dashboard-data.ts`) — there is no real
  auth/session or papers API to source it from yet.

content.text: Found a real production-build gap: `apps/api`/`apps/worker` compiled to plain JS via `tsc`, but `@relis/config` only ships TypeScript source, so Node's ESM loader can't resolve it at runtime (`node dist/main.js` fails). Since no bundler is mandated for the backend, I'll run these processes via `tsx` for both dev and start, avoiding a fragile dual dist pipeline.

## Why api/worker run via `tsx`, not compiled `dist/`

`@relis/config` ships as TypeScript source (consumed directly by `tsx` in
apps/api and apps/worker, and by Next.js in apps/web via
`transpilePackages`). No bundler is mandated for the backend in
`stack.yml`, so `apps/api`/`apps/worker`'s `build` script only type-checks
(`tsc --noEmit`) and `start` runs the TypeScript source directly through
`tsx` — the same way `dev` does. A plain `tsc`-to-`dist/` + `node dist/main.js`
pipeline was tried first and does not work as-is: Node's ESM loader cannot
resolve the extensionless relative imports inside `@relis/config`'s
TypeScript source, so `node dist/main.js` fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`
unless `@relis/config` is also compiled to a separate `dist/`. Using `tsx`
for both dev and start avoids that extra build target.

# relis

pnpm workspace monorepo for the ReLiS application, following
[`../rules and context/project-structure.md`](../rules%20and%20context/project-structure.md)
and [`../rules and context/stack.yml`](../rules%20and%20context/stack.yml).

This is a minimal foundation created to support runtime configuration
validation (see `packages/config`). It intentionally does not yet include
a database schema, job queue, storage, auth, or CI/CD pipeline — those are
separate backlog items and out of scope here.

## Layout

```
relis/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ web/     Next.js App Router frontend. Shared layout + home page only,
│  │           adapted from v1/. See apps/web/src/shared/lib/mock-dashboard-data.ts
│  │           for the placeholder data it renders.
│  ├─ api/     Hono API. Entry point + health/readiness routes only — no
│  │           business modules yet.
│  └─ worker/  Minimal worker process shell — no job/queue processing yet.
├─ packages/
│  └─ config/  Shared, Zod-validated environment configuration contract
│              used by web, api, worker, and (once they exist) migration
│              and deployment tooling. See packages/config/README.md.
├─ .env.example
├─ pnpm-workspace.yaml
└─ tsconfig.base.json
```

## Scripts (run from `relis/`)

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck   # tsc --noEmit in every package/app
pnpm test        # vitest run in every package/app
pnpm build       # build every package/app
pnpm dev         # run web/api/worker dev servers in parallel
pnpm check:env -- <process>   # validate one process's env without starting it
```

Or scope any of the above to one project: `pnpm --filter @relis/api run test`.

## Environment configuration

Every process validates its own required environment variables before doing
any operational work (accepting HTTP traffic, processing jobs, or running
migrations), through the shared contract in `packages/config`. See:

- `packages/config/README.md` — variables, categories, per-process
  requirements, error codes.
- `.env.example` — safe example values (no real credentials).

## Known gaps

- **Migration tooling**: no `packages/database` Prisma schema exists yet,
  so `loadMigrationConfig()` (in `packages/config`) is defined but not
  called from any actual migration script.
- **Deployment**: no CI/CD pipeline or Docker Compose exists yet. A future
  pipeline can call `pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- <process>`
  once one is built.
- **apps/web**: only the shared layout and home/dashboard page were ported
  from `v1/`; all other v1 pages (login, screening, quality assessment,
  data extraction, reports) were intentionally not migrated. The home page
  renders mock data (`mock-dashboard-data.ts`) — there is no real
  auth/session or papers API to source it from yet.

Everything is in order. Here's the summary report.

## What was implemented

**Blocker resolved first:** `relis/` had no monorepo foundation at all (no `package.json`, no apps, no packages). You authorized creating the minimal foundation plus a limited v1 frontend port; everything below stayed inside that authorization.

### Workspace foundation
`relis/package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `tsconfig.base.json`, `.gitignore`, `.env.example` — pnpm workspaces, TypeScript, Zod/Vitest per `stack.yml`.

### `packages/config` — the config contract (core deliverable)
- `variables.ts`: single source of truth for every env var (`NODE_ENV`, `PORT`, `DATABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`), each tagged with category + secrecy.
- `processes/{api,worker,web,migration}.ts`: Zod schemas composed per-process from those variables — worker has no `PORT`, web-public has no `DATABASE_URL`, migration has only `DATABASE_URL`.
- `errors.ts`/`validate.ts`: `ConfigValidationError` whose message/issues/`toSafeDiagnostics()` carry only variable name + category + a stable code (`CONFIG_MISSING`/`CONFIG_INVALID`) — never the value.
- `web-public.ts`: separate browser-safe entry point (no secret schema reachable from it).
- `cli.ts`: standalone `check:env <process>` validator for future deployment pipelines (not wired to any pipeline — none exists).
- No queue/broker variable was added — `background_jobs` is still `undecided` in `stack.yml` (pg-boss vs BullMQ), per PENDING-DECISIONS #1.

### `apps/api` (Hono)
`main.ts` validates config before `serve()` starts; exits 1 with safe diagnostics on failure. `platform/http/health.ts` adds `/health/live` (liveness only) and `/health/ready` (safe config categories, no values).

### `apps/worker`
`main.ts` validates config before doing anything else; exits 1 on failure, otherwise logs and idles (no job/queue processing implemented).

### `apps/web` (Next.js App Router)
Adapted from `v1/` (unchanged, verified via `git diff`): `AppShell` (sidebar/nav) and the home/dashboard page, using `mock-dashboard-data.ts` (explicitly labeled mock). `src/instrumentation.ts` validates both server and public config before the server accepts requests, exiting 1 on failure. `middleware.ts` + `[locale]` routing + minimal `en`/`fr` dictionaries per `project-structure.md`.

## Verification actually run
- `pnpm -r run typecheck` — all 4 projects pass.
- `pnpm -r run test` (Vitest) — **21/21 tests pass**: valid config, missing/invalid values, process-specific requirements, public/server separation, no-value-leak diagnostics, live vs ready health routes, and real subprocess startup tests (`tsx` spawning `main.ts`) proving invalid config exits non-zero before any server binds, and valid config actually serves traffic.
- `pnpm -r run build` — api/worker typecheck-as-build, `next build` succeeds and prerenders `/en`, `/fr`.
- Manually verified `next start`/`api start`/`worker start` both fail closed (exit 1, safe JSON diagnostics, nothing exposed) on missing config and serve/idle correctly on valid config.
- Found and fixed a real gap along the way: compiling api/worker to `dist/` broke at runtime because Node's ESM loader can't resolve `@relis/config`'s TypeScript source — switched `build`/`start` to typecheck+`tsx` (documented in `relis/README.md`).

## Gaps / not implemented (reported, not built)
- **Migration**: `loadMigrationConfig()` exists but isn't called anywhere — no `packages/database` Prisma schema exists yet.
- **Deployment**: no CI/CD or Docker Compose exists; the `check:env` CLI is available for a future pipeline to call.
- `apps/web` ports only the shared layout + home page from v1 — login/screening/QA/data-extraction/reports pages were intentionally not migrated.

Define one typed environment configuration contract for web, API, worker, migration, and deployment processes, and fail fast before accepting traffic or writing data when required configuration is absent or invalid.

First read CLAUDE.md and the mandatory references in rules and context, particularly project-structure.md and stack.yml. All implementation must remain inside relis/. Treat notion-tasks as reference only, not authorization to implement additional features.

You are authorized to fix the issues below and add the minimum migration and deployment integration necessary to satisfy this task. Do not implement unrelated business features, database domain models, queue processing, additional frontend pages, or other backlog tasks. Preserve existing user changes and keep v1 unchanged.

1. Validate frontend configuration before server startup

The current apps/web/src/instrumentation.ts validation runs too late:
- With NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL missing, the Next server briefly accepts TCP connections before exiting.
- With PORT=0, Next selects a port and replaces process.env.PORT before validation, bypassing the contract’s minimum-port requirement.

Implement a preflight startup mechanism that validates configuration before Next opens a listener or normalizes away invalid input. Cover supported development and production startup commands. Preserve appropriate .env loading semantics and validate the effective configuration, including supported command-line overrides.

Instrumentation may remain as defense in depth, but must not be the sole startup gate.

2. Strengthen URL validation

packages/config/src/primitives.ts currently accepts invalid database connection strings, including:
- postgresql://user:pass@
- postgresql://localhost:99999/db

Replace the prefix-only validation with structural validation appropriate to the PostgreSQL connection formats supported by the prescribed database tooling. Validate scheme, host and port where applicable without rejecting legitimate supported connection options.

NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL currently accepts javascript: and file: URLs. Restrict it to HTTP/HTTPS URLs with a valid host and reject embedded credentials.

Never include rejected values, credentials, or raw parser errors in diagnostics.

3. Fix browser-public configuration loading

loadWebPublicConfig() currently defaults to the entire process.env object, which does not support Next’s static inlining of public environment variables.

Use explicit public-variable references or an explicitly constructed public configuration object. Keep the browser entry point isolated from server-only configuration and secrets.

Define and document the distinction between:
- Public values embedded during build.
- Server values validated at runtime.

Validate public configuration before building the frontend. Do not claim that changing startup environment variables changes values already embedded in the client bundle.

Add a test exercising actual client bundling, not only schema parsing with a manually supplied object.

4. Reject unsupported CLI targets

The following command currently exits successfully without validating configuration:
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- toString

Use an explicit allowlist, Map, or own-property check. Unsupported targets, including toString, constructor and __proto__, must produce safe diagnostics and a nonzero exit code.

5. Implement the minimal migration integration

Inspect the prescribed database stack and project structure. Add the smallest executable migration entry point needed to invoke the selected migration tooling.

Requirements:
- Load the shared migration configuration before creating a database client, opening a connection, or invoking migration operations.
- Missing or invalid configuration must prevent all database activity.
- Use the validated configuration for the operation.
- Wire a documented workspace command to this entry point.
- Do not invent business tables, domain models, seed data, or unrelated migrations merely to demonstrate the integration.
- Test ordering with a spy or controlled substitute, and test the real command’s invalid-configuration exit behavior.

If the database tooling requires minimal configuration scaffolding, it is authorized within this task. If a genuine architectural decision is unresolved by the project references, ask a targeted question instead of silently choosing.

6. Implement the minimal deployment validation gate

A standalone optional check:env command is not sufficient integration.

Add a concrete, documented deployment entry point appropriate to the existing repository and prescribed stack. Configuration validation must be a mandatory step before any deployment action that starts services or writes data, including migrations.

Do not introduce a cloud provider, full CI/CD platform, or Docker architecture unless already prescribed and necessary. A minimal local deployment orchestration command is acceptable if no deployment infrastructure exists.

Requirements:
- Validate all processes involved in the selected deployment before performing its first side effect.
- Respect process-specific environments and frontend build-time versus runtime configuration.
- Stop on failure and propagate nonzero exit codes.
- Do not create another no-op validator and describe it as completed deployment integration.
- Test that failed preflight prevents every downstream action.

7. Verification and documentation

Add regression tests covering:
- Invalid PostgreSQL and public API URLs.
- Browser-public configuration loading and exclusion of secrets.
- Unsupported CLI targets.
- Frontend invalid configuration exiting before any listener opens.
- PORT=0 being rejected rather than normalized into an accepted value.
- Valid frontend startup.
- Migration validation occurring before any database activity.
- Deployment validation occurring before downstream actions.
- Safe diagnostics containing categories and stable codes, but no configuration values.

Keep and rerun the existing tests. Run typecheck, tests and builds. Use dummy configuration values; do not access real infrastructure or run a real deployment without separate authorization.

Update relevant documentation and .env examples to explain the actual commands, loading behavior, defaults, required variables, and build-time/runtime distinction. Keep documentation in English.

Completion criteria:
All five process categories must have executable integration with the shared typed contract. Missing or invalid required configuration must block traffic or data-writing actions as appropriate. Passing schema unit tests alone is not sufficient.

In your final report:
- List changes and commands executed.
- Distinguish verified behavior from assumptions or untested external integrations.
- Explain how each process satisfies the requirement.
- Identify any remaining blockers honestly; do not mark the task complete if required integrations remain absent.

input.new_string:
/**
 * Defense-in-depth only. The primary, documented startup gate is
 * ../scripts/preflight.ts, which validates configuration *before* the
 * `next` process is even spawned — required because PORT=0/Next's own
 * listener timing make an in-process check here alone insufficient (see
 * preflight.ts's header comment). This hook still runs once when the
 * Next.js server process starts (dev and prod, Node runtime), so it also
 * catches anything that invokes `next` directly, bypassing preflight.
 * Deliberately unconditional (checks both server and public config
 * regardless of dev/prod) rather than mirroring preflight's build-vs-start
 * distinction: as a safety net it's better to fail loudly here if a
 * runtime environment is missing something the build-time environment had,
 * rather than risk a later crash.
 */

content.text: Now let's update all the documentation. First `packages/config/README.md`.

content.content:
1	# @relis/config
2	
3	Single, typed, Zod-validated environment configuration contract shared by
4	`apps/web`, `apps/api`, `apps/worker`, migration tooling, and deployment
5	scripts. Each consumer imports only the loader for its own process, so it
6	never requires or receives configuration it doesn't need.
7	
8	## Variables
9	
10	| Variable | Category | Secret | Required by | Validation |
11	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
12	| `NODE_ENV` | `core` | no | api, worker, web (server) | one of `development`, `test`, `production`; defaults to `development` |
13	| `PORT` | `network` | no | api (default `3001`), web server (default `3000`) | digits only, coerced to an integer in `1..65535` |
14	| `DATABASE_URL` | `database` | **yes** | api, worker, migration | non-empty string matching `postgres(ql)://...` |
15	| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `web-public` | no | web (browser) | absolute URL; inlined into the client bundle by Next.js at build time |
16	
17	Every variable is declared once in `src/variables.ts`, including its
18	category and secrecy flag; process schemas in `src/processes/*.ts` compose
19	the subset each process actually needs.
20	
21	## Process-specific contracts
22	
23	| Process | Schema | Notes |
24	| --- | --- | --- |
25	| `api` | `apiSchema` (`src/processes/api.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT` + `DATABASE_URL`. |
26	| `worker` | `workerSchema` (`src/processes/worker.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `DATABASE_URL`. No `PORT` — the worker has no HTTP surface. No queue/broker variable yet: `background_jobs` is still `undecided` (pg-boss vs. BullMQ) in `stack.yml`. |
27	| `web` (browser) | `webPublicSchema` (`src/processes/web.ts`) | Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`. Never includes `DATABASE_URL` or any other secret. Import via `@relis/config/web-public`, not `@relis/config`. |
28	| `web` (server) | `webServerSchema` | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT`. Still no secrets — the Next.js server in this repository does not talk to the database directly. |
29	| `migration` | `migrationSchema` (`src/processes/migration.ts`) | `DATABASE_URL` only. Not yet called from a real migration script — see the repository-level implementation report; no `packages/database` Prisma schema exists yet. |
30	
31	## Usage
32	
33	```ts
34	// apps/api/src/main.ts
35	import { loadApiConfig, ConfigValidationError } from "@relis/config";
36	
37	try {
38	  const config = loadApiConfig(); // reads process.env
39	  // ... start the server with config.PORT / config.DATABASE_URL

# @relis/config

Single, typed, Zod-validated environment configuration contract shared by
`apps/web`, `apps/api`, `apps/worker`, migration tooling, and deployment
scripts. Each consumer imports only the loader for its own process, so it
never requires or receives configuration it doesn't need.

## Variables

| Variable | Category | Secret | Required by | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_ENV` | `core` | no | api, worker, web (server) | one of `development`, `test`, `production`; defaults to `development` |
| `PORT` | `network` | no | api (default `3001`), web server (default `3000`) | digits only, coerced to an integer in `1..65535` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `database` | **yes** | api, worker, migration | non-empty string matching `postgres(ql)://...` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `web-public` | no | web (browser) | absolute URL; inlined into the client bundle by Next.js at build time |

Every variable is declared once in `src/variables.ts`, including its
category and secrecy flag; process schemas in `src/processes/*.ts` compose
the subset each process actually needs.

## Process-specific contracts

| Process | Schema | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api` | `apiSchema` (`src/processes/api.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT` + `DATABASE_URL`. |
| `worker` | `workerSchema` (`src/processes/worker.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `DATABASE_URL`. No `PORT` — the worker has no HTTP surface. No queue/broker variable yet: `background_jobs` is still `undecided` (pg-boss vs. BullMQ) in `stack.yml`. |
| `web` (browser) | `webPublicSchema` (`src/processes/web.ts`) | Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`. Never includes `DATABASE_URL` or any other secret. Import via `@relis/config/web-public`, not `@relis/config`. |
| `web` (server) | `webServerSchema` | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT`. Still no secrets — the Next.js server in this repository does not talk to the database directly. |
| `migration` | `migrationSchema` (`src/processes/migration.ts`) | `DATABASE_URL` only. Not yet called from a real migration script — see the repository-level implementation report; no `packages/database` Prisma schema exists yet. |

## Usage

```ts
// apps/api/src/main.ts
import { loadApiConfig, ConfigValidationError } from "@relis/config";

try {
  const config = loadApiConfig(); // reads process.env
  // ... start the server with config.PORT / config.DATABASE_URL
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof ConfigValidationError) {
    console.error(JSON.stringify(error.toSafeDiagnostics()));
    process.exit(1);
  }
  throw error;
}
```

```ts
// a client component in apps/web
import { loadWebPublicConfig } from "@relis/config/web-public";

const { NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL } = loadWebPublicConfig();
```

## Errors and diagnostics

A failed `load*Config()` call throws `ConfigValidationError`. Its `message`,
`issues`, and `toSafeDiagnostics()` only ever contain:

- the **variable name** (e.g. `DATABASE_URL`),
- its **category** (`core` | `network` | `database` | `web-public`), and
- a **stable code**: `CONFIG_MISSING` or `CONFIG_INVALID`.

The raw value is never read into any of these — safe to log or return from
an HTTP diagnostics endpoint as-is.

## Deployment / CI validation

No CI/CD pipeline exists yet in this repository. `src/cli.ts` is a
standalone entry point a future pipeline can shell out to without waiting
on one to be built:

```sh
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- api
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- worker
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- web-public
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- web-server
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- migration
```

Exits `0` with `{"status":"valid"}` or `1` with safe diagnostics.

## Example values

See `relis/.env.example` at the workspace root for safe, non-real sample
values for every variable above.

# @relis/config

Single, typed, Zod-validated environment configuration contract shared by
`apps/web`, `apps/api`, `apps/worker`, `packages/database` (migrations),
and `tooling` (deployment). Each consumer imports only the loader for its
own process, so it never requires or receives configuration it doesn't
need.

## Variables

| Variable | Category | Secret | Required by | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_ENV` | `core` | no | api, worker, web (server) | one of `development`, `test`, `production`; defaults to `development` |
| `PORT` | `network` | no | api (default `3001`), web server (default `3000`) | digits only, coerced to an integer in `1..65535`. `PORT=0` ("let the OS pick a free port") is intentionally rejected — the contract requires an explicit port. |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `database` | **yes** | api, worker, migration | structurally validated with the WHATWG `URL` parser (not a prefix regex): scheme must be `postgres:` or `postgresql:`, and there must be a host — either a normal network host, or a Unix-socket `?host=/path` query parameter (Prisma's documented form for that case). An out-of-range port (e.g. `:99999`) or an empty host (e.g. `postgresql://user:pass@`) is rejected. |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `web-public` | no | web (browser) | absolute **http(s)** URL with a real host and **no embedded credentials**; inlined into the client bundle by Next.js at build time. `javascript:`, `file:`, and `user:pass@host` URLs are rejected. |

Every variable is declared once in `src/variables.ts`, including its
category and secrecy flag; process schemas in `src/processes/*.ts` compose
the subset each process actually needs.

## Process-specific contracts

| Process | Schema | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api` | `apiSchema` (`src/processes/api.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT` + `DATABASE_URL`. |
| `worker` | `workerSchema` (`src/processes/worker.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `DATABASE_URL`. No `PORT` — the worker has no HTTP surface. No queue/broker variable yet: `background_jobs` is still `undecided` (pg-boss vs. BullMQ) in `stack.yml`. |
| `web` (browser) | `webPublicSchema` (`src/processes/web.ts`) | Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`. Never includes `DATABASE_URL` or any other secret. Import via `@relis/config/web-public`, not `@relis/config`. |
| `web` (server) | `webServerSchema` | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT`. Still no secrets — the Next.js server in this repository does not talk to the database directly. |
| `migration` | `migrationSchema` (`src/processes/migration.ts`) | `DATABASE_URL` only. Called for real by `packages/database`'s `pnpm run migrate` — see that package's README. |

`loadAllConfigs()` (`src/load-all.ts`) validates every process above
against the same environment and aggregates every failing variable across
every process into one `ConfigValidationError` (`process: "deploy"`),
instead of stopping at the first failure — used by the deployment gate in
`tooling/scripts/deploy.ts`, which needs to report everything wrong before
doing anything.

## Build-time vs. runtime configuration (apps/web)

`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` and `PORT`/`NODE_ENV` are validated at **different
times**, because they matter at different times:

- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` is a build-time value.** Next.js inlines it
  literally into the compiled client JavaScript when you run `next build`
  (or on every recompile in `next dev`). Once built, that value is baked
  into the shipped bundle — changing the environment variable afterward,
  including at `next start` time, does **not** change what's already in
  the browser's JavaScript. So `apps/web/scripts/preflight.ts` validates it
  at `build` and at `dev`, but deliberately **not** at `start`.
- **`PORT`/`NODE_ENV` are runtime values.** They matter only to the
  running Next.js server process, so they're validated at `dev` and
  `start` (whenever a listener is about to open), not at `build`.

This distinction is enforced by `apps/web/scripts/preflight.ts` — see that
file and `relis/README.md` for how it gates `next dev`/`next build`/`next
start`, including why validating from inside the Next.js process
(`apps/web/src/instrumentation.ts`) alone is not sufficient (`PORT=0`
gets silently rewritten by Next before an in-process check can see the
original value).

## Usage

```ts
// apps/api/src/main.ts
import { loadApiConfig, ConfigValidationError } from "@relis/config";

try {
  const config = loadApiConfig(); // reads process.env
  // ... start the server with config.PORT / config.DATABASE_URL
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof ConfigValidationError) {
    console.error(JSON.stringify(error.toSafeDiagnostics()));
    process.exit(1);
  }
  throw error;
}
```

```ts
// a client component in apps/web
import { loadWebPublicConfig } from "@relis/config/web-public";

const { NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL } = loadWebPublicConfig();
```

Note: `loadWebPublicConfig()`'s default argument reads
`process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` as a **static member expression** — that
exact pattern is what Next.js's compiler recognizes and replaces with a
literal value for the client bundle. Don't refactor a caller to pass the
whole `process.env` object (or destructure it) instead of calling
`loadWebPublicConfig()` bare — that pattern is not something Next.js can
statically inline, and `process.env` isn't even defined in the browser at
runtime. `apps/web/src/shared/lib/public-config.build.test.ts` is a real
`next build` + bundle-content assertion (not just a schema-parsing test)
that guards against this regressing silently.

## Errors and diagnostics

A failed `load*Config()` call throws `ConfigValidationError`. Its `message`,
`issues`, and `toSafeDiagnostics()` only ever contain:

- the **variable name** (e.g. `DATABASE_URL`),
- its **category** (`core` | `network` | `database` | `web-public`), and
- a **stable code**: `CONFIG_MISSING` or `CONFIG_INVALID`.

The raw value is never read into any of these — safe to log or return from
an HTTP diagnostics endpoint as-is. This is verified against real rejected
values (including ones containing credentials) in `src/primitives.test.ts`
and `src/load-all.test.ts`, not just asserted in a comment.

## Deployment / CI validation

`src/cli.ts` is a standalone validation entry point:

```sh
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- api
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- worker
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- web-public
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- web-server
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- migration
# from the repo root:
pnpm check:env -- api
```

Exits `0` with `{"status":"valid"}` or `1` with safe diagnostics. Targets
are looked up in a `Map`, not a plain object, so a prototype-derived name
(`toString`, `constructor`, `__proto__`, `hasOwnProperty`, ...) cannot be
silently "found" and treated as a validated process — it's rejected the
same as any other unknown target (see `src/cli.test.ts`).

This CLI alone is **not** the deployment integration for this repository —
it's a building block. The actual gate that gates build/migrate/start
behind validation is `tooling/scripts/deploy.ts`; see `relis/README.md`
and `tooling/README.md`.

## Example values

See `relis/.env.example` at the workspace root for safe, non-real sample
values for every variable above.

# @relis/config

Single, typed, Zod-validated environment configuration contract shared by
`apps/web`, `apps/api`, `apps/worker`, migration tooling, and deployment
scripts. Each consumer imports only the loader for its own process, so it
never requires or receives configuration it doesn't need.

## Variables

| Variable | Category | Secret | Required by | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_ENV` | `core` | no | api, worker, web (server) | one of `development`, `test`, `production`; defaults to `development` |
| `PORT` | `network` | no | api (default `3001`), web server (default `3000`) | digits only, coerced to an integer in `1..65535` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `database` | **yes** | api, worker, migration | non-empty string matching `postgres(ql)://...` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `web-public` | no | web (browser) | absolute URL; inlined into the client bundle by Next.js at build time |

Every variable is declared once in `src/variables.ts`, including its
category and secrecy flag; process schemas in `src/processes/*.ts` compose
the subset each process actually needs.

## Process-specific contracts

| Process | Schema | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api` | `apiSchema` (`src/processes/api.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT` + `DATABASE_URL`. |
| `worker` | `workerSchema` (`src/processes/worker.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `DATABASE_URL`. No `PORT` — the worker has no HTTP surface. No queue/broker variable yet: `background_jobs` is still `undecided` (pg-boss vs. BullMQ) in `stack.yml`. |
| `web` (browser) | `webPublicSchema` (`src/processes/web.ts`) | Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`. Never includes `DATABASE_URL` or any other secret. Import via `@relis/config/web-public`, not `@relis/config`. |
| `web` (server) | `webServerSchema` | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT`. Still no secrets — the Next.js server in this repository does not talk to the database directly. |
| `migration` | `migrationSchema` (`src/processes/migration.ts`) | `DATABASE_URL` only. Not yet called from a real migration script — see the repository-level implementation report; no `packages/database` Prisma schema exists yet. |

## Usage

```ts
// apps/api/src/main.ts
import { loadApiConfig, ConfigValidationError } from "@relis/config";

try {
  const config = loadApiConfig(); // reads process.env
  // ... start the server with config.PORT / config.DATABASE_URL
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof ConfigValidationError) {
    console.error(JSON.stringify(error.toSafeDiagnostics()));
    process.exit(1);
  }
  throw error;
}
```

```ts
// a client component in apps/web
import { loadWebPublicConfig } from "@relis/config/web-public";

const { NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL } = loadWebPublicConfig();
```

## Errors and diagnostics

A failed `load*Config()` call throws `ConfigValidationError`. Its `message`,
`issues`, and `toSafeDiagnostics()` only ever contain:

- the **variable name** (e.g. `DATABASE_URL`),
- its **category** (`core` | `network` | `database` | `web-public`), and
- a **stable code**: `CONFIG_MISSING` or `CONFIG_INVALID`.

The raw value is never read into any of these — safe to log or return from
an HTTP diagnostics endpoint as-is.

## Deployment / CI validation

No CI/CD pipeline exists yet in this repository. `src/cli.ts` is a
standalone entry point a future pipeline can shell out to without waiting
on one to be built:

```sh
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- api
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- worker
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- web-public
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- web-server
pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- migration
```

Exits `0` with `{"status":"valid"}` or `1` with safe diagnostics.

## Example values

See `relis/.env.example` at the workspace root for safe, non-real sample
values for every variable above.

# @relis/database

Minimal, real migration entry point for the **control** PostgreSQL
database (`stack.yml`: PostgreSQL + Prisma). This package intentionally
contains no domain models, business tables, or seed data — it exists to
satisfy "runtime config validation must gate migrations", not to implement
the control database's actual schema (a separate backlog task).

## What's here

- `prisma/control/schema.prisma` — a Prisma schema with a `datasource` and
  `generator` block and **zero models**. Enough for the Prisma CLI to be
  invoked against; not a data model.
- `src/migrate.ts` — `runMigration(deps?)`. Validates configuration via
  `loadMigrationConfig()` from `@relis/config` **before** creating any
  database client, opening a connection, or invoking Prisma. If validation
  fails, `runPrisma` is never called — no database activity happens at
  all. Dependencies (`loadConfig`, `runPrisma`) are injectable so this can
  be tested for ordering with spies, without a real Postgres instance.
- `src/run-migrate.ts` — the real CLI entry point: `process.exit(runMigration())`.
- `src/index.ts` — re-exports `runMigration`/`defaultRunPrisma` for
  programmatic use (the deployment gate in `tooling/` imports this
  directly rather than shelling out).

## Running it

```sh
# from this package:
pnpm run migrate
# from the repo root:
pnpm run migrate
```

Requires `DATABASE_URL` (control database). On success, runs
`prisma migrate deploy --schema prisma/control/schema.prisma`
non-interactively, using the already-validated connection string. On
missing/invalid configuration, exits non-zero with safe diagnostics
(variable name + category + code — never the value) and never reaches
Prisma at all.

## What this does NOT do

- No `project` schema (per-project databases, `stack.yml`'s
  `schema_strategy: [control, project]`) — that's the project-database
  resolver task, out of scope here.
- No domain tables/migrations were written; `prisma migrate deploy`
  against the current empty schema has nothing to apply.
- Never run against real infrastructure by this change — only tested with
  dummy `DATABASE_URL` values and a spied-out `runPrisma`. Running it
  against a real database requires separate authorization.

# @relis/tooling

`scripts/deploy.ts` — the minimal, **local** deployment orchestration
entry point for this repository. No CI/CD platform, cloud provider, or
container/Docker architecture exists here yet (see the root README's
"Known gaps"), so this Node script is the deployment integration for now,
per the task's "a minimal local deployment orchestration command is
acceptable if no deployment infrastructure exists."

## What it does, in order

1. **Validate.** `loadAllConfigs()` (from `@relis/config`) validates every
   process involved — api, worker, web server, web public, migration — as
   one aggregated pass, and reports every failing variable at once. This
   runs before anything else; on failure, safe diagnostics go to stderr and
   the process exits non-zero without touching the filesystem, a database,
   or a port.
2. **Build the web app.** Runs `apps/web`'s own preflight-gated `build`
   (`tsx apps/web/scripts/preflight.ts build`) — this is where
   `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` gets embedded into the client bundle. Stops here
   (propagating the exit code) if it fails.
3. **Migrate.** Calls `runMigration()` from `@relis/database` in-process —
   the control database's only side effect that writes anything. Stops
   here if it fails.
4. **Start services.** Spawns `apps/api`, `apps/worker`, and the now-built
   `apps/web` (`next start`) concurrently. Each has its own startup
   validation gate too (`main.ts` / `preflight.ts`) — this step launches
   them once every prior gate has already passed.

Each step is injectable (`DeployDeps` in `scripts/run-deploy.ts`), so the
ordering and short-circuit-on-failure behavior is tested with spies
(`scripts/run-deploy.test.ts`) — no real build, database, or running
service required for that — plus `scripts/deploy.startup.test.ts`, which
runs the **real** `deploy.ts` command with missing/invalid configuration
and asserts it exits non-zero before any build/migrate/start side effect
(checked by asserting none of their telltale output ever appears).

## Running it

```sh
# from this package:
pnpm run deploy
# from the repo root:
pnpm run deploy
```

## What this does NOT do

- Does not introduce a cloud provider, CI/CD platform, or Docker/container
  architecture — none is prescribed, and the task explicitly says not to
  add one unless necessary.
- Was never run end-to-end against a real database or with real services
  actually accepting traffic during this change — only its ordering (via
  spies) and its real invalid-configuration exit behavior were verified.
  Running a real deploy requires separate authorization.

# relis

pnpm workspace monorepo for the ReLiS application, following
[`../rules and context/project-structure.md`](../rules%20and%20context/project-structure.md)
and [`../rules and context/stack.yml`](../rules%20and%20context/stack.yml).

This is a minimal foundation created to support runtime configuration
validation (see `packages/config`). It intentionally does not yet include
a database schema, job queue, storage, auth, or CI/CD pipeline — those are
separate backlog items and out of scope here.

## Layout

```
relis/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ web/     Next.js App Router frontend. Shared layout + home page only,
│  │           adapted from v1/. See apps/web/src/shared/lib/mock-dashboard-data.ts
│  │           for the placeholder data it renders.
│  ├─ api/     Hono API. Entry point + health/readiness routes only — no
│  │           business modules yet.
│  └─ worker/  Minimal worker process shell — no job/queue processing yet.
├─ packages/
│  └─ config/  Shared, Zod-validated environment configuration contract
│              used by web, api, worker, and (once they exist) migration
│              and deployment tooling. See packages/config/README.md.
├─ .env.example
├─ pnpm-workspace.yaml
└─ tsconfig.base.json
```

## Scripts (run from `relis/`)

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck   # tsc --noEmit in every package/app
pnpm test        # vitest run in every package/app
pnpm build       # build every package/app
pnpm dev         # run web/api/worker dev servers in parallel
pnpm check:env -- <process>   # validate one process's env without starting it
```

Or scope any of the above to one project: `pnpm --filter @relis/api run test`.

## Environment configuration

Every process validates its own required environment variables before doing
any operational work (accepting HTTP traffic, processing jobs, or running
migrations), through the shared contract in `packages/config`. See:

- `packages/config/README.md` — variables, categories, per-process
  requirements, error codes.
- `.env.example` — safe example values (no real credentials).

## Why api/worker run via `tsx`, not compiled `dist/`

`@relis/config` ships as TypeScript source (consumed directly by `tsx` in
apps/api and apps/worker, and by Next.js in apps/web via
`transpilePackages`). No bundler is mandated for the backend in
`stack.yml`, so `apps/api`/`apps/worker`'s `build` script only type-checks
(`tsc --noEmit`) and `start` runs the TypeScript source directly through
`tsx` — the same way `dev` does. A plain `tsc`-to-`dist/` + `node dist/main.js`
pipeline was tried first and does not work as-is: Node's ESM loader cannot
resolve the extensionless relative imports inside `@relis/config`'s
TypeScript source, so `node dist/main.js` fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`
unless `@relis/config` is also compiled to a separate `dist/`. Using `tsx`
for both dev and start avoids that extra build target.

## Known gaps

- **Migration tooling**: no `packages/database` Prisma schema exists yet,
  so `loadMigrationConfig()` (in `packages/config`) is defined but not
  called from any actual migration script.
- **Deployment**: no CI/CD pipeline or Docker Compose exists yet. A future
  pipeline can call `pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- <process>`
  once one is built.
- **apps/web**: only the shared layout and home/dashboard page were ported
  from `v1/`; all other v1 pages (login, screening, quality assessment,
  data extraction, reports) were intentionally not migrated. The home page
  renders mock data (`mock-dashboard-data.ts`) — there is no real
  auth/session or papers API to source it from yet.

[`../rules and context/project-structure.md`](../rules%20and%20context/project-structure.md)
and [`../rules and context/stack.yml`](../rules%20and%20context/stack.yml).

validation (see `packages/config`), plus the smallest real migration and

intentionally does not yet include a real database schema, job queue,
storage, auth, or CI/CD pipeline — those are separate backlog items and
out of scope here.

## Layout

```
relis/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ web/       Next.js App Router frontend. Shared layout + home page only,
│  │             adapted from v1/. dev/build/start all run through
│  │             scripts/preflight.ts (see below), not `next` directly.
│  ├─ api/       Hono API. Entry point + health/readiness routes only — no
│  │             business modules yet.
│  └─ worker/    Minimal worker process shell — no job/queue processing yet.
├─ packages/
│  ├─ config/    Shared, Zod-validated environment configuration contract
│  │             used by web, api, worker, migration, and deployment.
│  │             See packages/config/README.md.
│  └─ database/  Minimal, real Prisma migration entry point for the control
│                database (no domain models). See packages/database/README.md.
├─ tooling/
│  └─ scripts/   deploy.ts — the local deployment orchestration gate.
│                See tooling/README.md.
├─ .env.example
├─ pnpm-workspace.yaml
└─ tsconfig.base.json
```

## Scripts (run from `relis/`)

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck   # tsc --noEmit in every package/app
pnpm test        # vitest run in every package/app
pnpm build       # build every package/app (apps/web's build validates NEXT_PUBLIC_*)
pnpm dev         # run web/api/worker dev servers in parallel
pnpm check:env -- <process>   # validate one process's env without starting it
pnpm migrate     # validate migration config, then run control-DB migrations
pnpm deploy      # validate everything, then build web -> migrate -> start services
```

Or scope any of the above to one project: `pnpm --filter @relis/api run test`.

## Environment configuration

Every process validates its own required environment variables before doing
any operational work (accepting HTTP traffic, processing jobs, running
migrations, or starting a deployment), through the shared contract in
`packages/config`. See:

  requirements, error codes, and the build-time-vs-runtime distinction for
  `apps/web`.
- `.env.example` — safe example values (no real credentials).

## apps/web: why `dev`/`build`/`start` go through `scripts/preflight.ts`

`apps/web/package.json`'s `dev`/`build`/`start` scripts run
`tsx scripts/preflight.ts <mode>`, not `next <mode>` directly.
`preflight.ts` validates configuration and only then spawns `next` as a
child process — validation happens **before** Next.js is even started, not
from inside it. This matters for two concrete bugs that validating only
from `apps/web/src/instrumentation.ts` (which still runs too, as a
secondary safety net) could not catch:

- **`PORT=0`.** Node/Next treat `PORT=0` as "ask the OS for any free port"
  and overwrite `process.env.PORT` with whatever they got — *before*
  `instrumentation.ts` (which runs inside the already-started Next process)
  gets a chance to see the original `"0"` and reject it per the contract's
  minimum-port rule. `preflight.ts` validates the raw/effective `PORT`
  (env var or a `-p`/`--port` CLI override — same precedence Next itself
  uses) strictly before Next is spawned at all, so the original invalid
  value is what actually gets checked.
- **A listener opening before rejection.** Refusing to spawn `next` at all
  on invalid configuration means no TCP listener ever opens, full stop —
  there's no window where Next has already started accepting connections
  before an in-process check can reject and exit.

documented in `packages/config/README.md`: `build` validates only
`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` (it never opens a listener), `dev` validates both
public and server config (it does both on every run), and `start`
validates only server config (`PORT`/`NODE_ENV`) — **not**
`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`, because by `start` time that value is already
embedded in the built client bundle and re-checking it at runtime would
incorrectly imply that changing it now could change already-shipped
browser JavaScript.

- **Migration**: `packages/database`'s `pnpm run migrate` (also `pnpm
  migrate` from the root) validates `DATABASE_URL` via
  `loadMigrationConfig()` before creating any database client or invoking
  Prisma, then runs `prisma migrate deploy` against a minimal, model-free
  control schema. See `packages/database/README.md`.
- **Deployment**: `tooling`'s `pnpm run deploy` (also `pnpm deploy` from
  the root) is the local deployment orchestration gate: validate every
  process at once → build the web app (embeds `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`) → run
  migrations (the first data-writing action) → start api/worker/web. Any
  step failing stops every later step and propagates a nonzero exit code.
  See `tooling/README.md`.

were verified with dummy configuration values (ordering via spies, and the
real commands' invalid-configuration exit behavior for real). Running
either against a real database/deployment target needs separate
authorization.

  migration entry point. The `project` schema (`stack.yml`'s
  `schema_strategy: [control, project]`, per-project databases) is a
  separate, unimplemented task (the project-database resolver).
- **Deployment**: no CI/CD platform, cloud provider, or Docker/container
  architecture exists — `tooling/scripts/deploy.ts` is a local
  orchestration script, not a pipeline. It was authorized and built as
  exactly that ("a minimal local deployment orchestration command"), not
  as a substitute for a future CI/CD task.
- **apps/web**: only the shared layout and home/dashboard page were ported
  from `v1/`; all other v1 pages (login, screening, quality assessment,
  data extraction, reports) were intentionally not migrated. The home page
  renders mock data (`mock-dashboard-data.ts`) — there is no real
  auth/session or papers API to source it from yet.

# relis

pnpm workspace monorepo for the ReLiS application, following
[`../rules and context/project-structure.md`](../rules%20and%20context/project-structure.md)
and [`../rules and context/stack.yml`](../rules%20and%20context/stack.yml).

This is a minimal foundation created to support runtime configuration
validation (see `packages/config`). It intentionally does not yet include
a database schema, job queue, storage, auth, or CI/CD pipeline — those are
separate backlog items and out of scope here.

## Layout

```
relis/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ web/     Next.js App Router frontend. Shared layout + home page only,
│  │           adapted from v1/. See apps/web/src/shared/lib/mock-dashboard-data.ts
│  │           for the placeholder data it renders.
│  ├─ api/     Hono API. Entry point + health/readiness routes only — no
│  │           business modules yet.
│  └─ worker/  Minimal worker process shell — no job/queue processing yet.
├─ packages/
│  └─ config/  Shared, Zod-validated environment configuration contract
│              used by web, api, worker, and (once they exist) migration
│              and deployment tooling. See packages/config/README.md.
├─ .env.example
├─ pnpm-workspace.yaml
└─ tsconfig.base.json
```

## Scripts (run from `relis/`)

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck   # tsc --noEmit in every package/app
pnpm test        # vitest run in every package/app
pnpm build       # build every package/app
pnpm dev         # run web/api/worker dev servers in parallel
pnpm check:env -- <process>   # validate one process's env without starting it
```

Or scope any of the above to one project: `pnpm --filter @relis/api run test`.

## Environment configuration

Every process validates its own required environment variables before doing
any operational work (accepting HTTP traffic, processing jobs, or running
migrations), through the shared contract in `packages/config`. See:

- `packages/config/README.md` — variables, categories, per-process
  requirements, error codes.
- `.env.example` — safe example values (no real credentials).

## Why api/worker run via `tsx`, not compiled `dist/`

`@relis/config` ships as TypeScript source (consumed directly by `tsx` in
apps/api and apps/worker, and by Next.js in apps/web via
`transpilePackages`). No bundler is mandated for the backend in
`stack.yml`, so `apps/api`/`apps/worker`'s `build` script only type-checks
(`tsc --noEmit`) and `start` runs the TypeScript source directly through
`tsx` — the same way `dev` does. A plain `tsc`-to-`dist/` + `node dist/main.js`
pipeline was tried first and does not work as-is: Node's ESM loader cannot
resolve the extensionless relative imports inside `@relis/config`'s
TypeScript source, so `node dist/main.js` fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`
unless `@relis/config` is also compiled to a separate `dist/`. Using `tsx`
for both dev and start avoids that extra build target.

## Known gaps

- **Migration tooling**: no `packages/database` Prisma schema exists yet,
  so `loadMigrationConfig()` (in `packages/config`) is defined but not
  called from any actual migration script.
- **Deployment**: no CI/CD pipeline or Docker Compose exists yet. A future
  pipeline can call `pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- <process>`
  once one is built.
- **apps/web**: only the shared layout and home/dashboard page were ported
  from `v1/`; all other v1 pages (login, screening, quality assessment,
  data extraction, reports) were intentionally not migrated. The home page
  renders mock data (`mock-dashboard-data.ts`) — there is no real
  auth/session or papers API to source it from yet.

# Shared environment configuration contract — see packages/config/README.md

# Copy the variables a given process needs into its own .env (or your

# Loading: apps/web (via its scripts/preflight.ts wrapper around `next`)

# (.env.local, .env.<development|production>[.local], .env). apps/api,

NODE_ENV=development

# --- network (api, web server) -----------------------------------------
# API default: 3001. Web server default: 3000.
# PORT=0 ("let the OS pick a free port") is rejected — an explicit port is
# required. `next dev`/`next start`'s own -p/--port CLI flag, if given,
# overrides this and is what actually gets validated.
PORT=3001

# --- database (api, worker, migration) — SECRET, never expose to web ---
# Must be postgres:// or postgresql://, with either a normal host or a
# host= query parameter (Unix socket form, e.g. Cloud SQL):
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://relis:relis@localhost:5432/relis_control
# DATABASE_URL=postgresql://relis:relis@/relis_control?host=/cloudsql/project:region:instance

# BUILD-TIME value: inlined into the client bundle by `next build` (and on
# every recompile in `next dev`). Changing it after the app is built —
# including at `next start` — does NOT change what's already shipped to
# the browser; you must rebuild. Must be an absolute http(s) URL with a
# real host and no embedded credentials (javascript:, file:, and
# user:pass@host values are all rejected). Never a secret.
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3001

All clean (it's gitignored via `*.tsbuildinfo` anyway). Here's the final report.

## Report

### 1. Frontend preflight (fixed)
New `apps/web/scripts/preflight.ts` validates config **before spawning `next`** at all — `dev`/`build`/`start` now run `tsx scripts/preflight.ts <mode>` instead of `next <mode>` directly. It replicates Next's own `.env` loading (`@next/env`'s `loadEnvConfig`) and honors a `-p`/`--port` CLI override with the same precedence Next uses, so the *effective* value is what's checked. `instrumentation.ts` stays as a documented secondary safety net (unconditional), not the sole gate.
- **Verified real**: `PORT=0` rejected before Next ever prints its banner (no listener opens); a CLI `--port 0` override is rejected even when `PORT` env is valid; a CLI `--port` override of a bad `PORT` env value is accepted; `build` validates only `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` (not `PORT`); `start` validates only server config (not `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`) — 9 tests in `scripts/preflight.test.ts`, all spawning the real script.

### 2. URL validation (fixed)
`primitives.ts` now parses with the WHATWG `URL` class instead of a prefix regex. `postgresql://user:pass@` and `postgresql://localhost:99999/db` are now rejected (empty host / out-of-range port); Unix-socket form (`?host=...`) still accepted. `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` now requires `http`/`https`, a real host, and no embedded credentials — `javascript:`, `file:`, and `user:pass@host` all rejected. 21 new tests in `primitives.test.ts`, all confirming no leaked values.

### 3. Browser-public config loading (fixed)
`loadWebPublicConfig()`'s default now reads `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` as a static reference (required for Next's build-time inlining), not the whole `process.env` object. Added `apps/web/src/shared/lib/public-config.ts` + a hidden diagnostic node in `AppShell`, and a **real** integration test (`public-config.build.test.ts`) that runs an actual `next build` with a sentinel URL and a decoy `DATABASE_URL`, then greps the emitted client chunks — confirms the sentinel is inlined and the secret is absent from real bundle bytes, not just schema parsing.

### 4. CLI safety (fixed)
`cli.ts` now uses a `Map` instead of a plain object, closing the `toString`/`constructor`/`__proto__`/`hasOwnProperty` prototype-pollution hole (previously exited 0 as "valid"). 7 tests confirm rejection with safe diagnostics.

### 5. Migration integration (new, real)
New `packages/database` package: minimal model-free `prisma/control/schema.prisma`, `runMigration()` (validates via `loadMigrationConfig()` before any Prisma invocation, injectable deps), and `pnpm migrate` from the root. Ordering proven with spies (no real DB); the real command's invalid-config exit path (missing and structurally-invalid `DATABASE_URL`) verified by spawning the actual script — 5 tests.

### 6. Deployment integration (new, real, local)
New `tooling` package: `pnpm deploy` runs `loadAllConfigs()` (aggregates issues across all 5 processes) → build web → migrate → start api/worker/web, stopping and propagating exit codes on any failure. No CI/CD/cloud/Docker introduced, per the constraint. Ordering/short-circuiting proven with spies; the real command's invalid-config path verified (asserts none of build/migrate/start's telltale output appears) — 6 tests.

### Verification actually run
- `pnpm -r run typecheck` — 6/6 projects clean.
- `pnpm -r run test` — **73/73 tests pass** (config 43, api 4, worker 2, database 5, web 13, tooling 6).
- `pnpm -r run build` — full build succeeds, including `apps/web`'s preflight-gated build.
- Manually re-verified from the repo root: `pnpm check:env -- api/toString`, `pnpm migrate`, `pnpm deploy` all block correctly with safe diagnostics on missing config (found and fixed an argv-forwarding bug from nested `pnpm --filter` invocation along the way).
- **Not run**: any command against a real Postgres instance or a real deployment — explicitly out of scope without separate authorization; only dummy values and spies were used.

### Honest limitations
- `packages/database` covers only the **control** schema; `project` (per-project DBs) is untouched.
- `tooling/scripts/deploy.ts`'s `startServices` step (real `spawn` of api/worker/web) is exercised only via injected fakes in tests — never run for real end-to-end in this session.
- v1/ confirmed unchanged (`git diff --stat -- v1` empty).

message.content:
1. Deployment lifecycle
- Start the frontend through its preflight, not directly through next start.
- Monitor child-process startup errors and exits.
- If a service fails, stop the other services and exit nonzero.
- Clean up child processes when deployment is interrupted.

2. Per-process configuration
- API and web currently inherit the same PORT, causing a conflict when PORT is explicitly set.
- Resolve and validate each service’s effective configuration before build or migration.
- Reject conflicting ports and pass the validated values to each service.

3. Frontend CLI parsing
- The preflight validates the first --port occurrence, but Next uses the last.
- Reproduction: start --port 41244 --port 0 passes validation and starts on a random port.
- Normalize arguments or reject conflicting options so Next uses exactly the port that was validated.

4. PostgreSQL socket URLs
- Reject malformed values currently accepted:

# Shared environment configuration contract — see packages/config/README.md
# for the full per-process breakdown, validation rules, and error codes.
#
# Copy the variables a given process needs into its own .env (or your
# process manager / deployment secrets store). Never commit a real .env.
#
# Loading: apps/web (via its scripts/preflight.ts wrapper around `next`)
# and Next.js itself both load .env files with Next's own precedence
# (.env.local, .env.<development|production>[.local], .env). apps/api,
# apps/worker, packages/database, and tooling read process.env directly —
# use your shell, a process manager, or `dotenv -e .env --` when running
# them locally; none of them load a .env file on their own.

# --- core (api, worker, web server) -----------------------------------
NODE_ENV=development

# --- network (api, web server) -----------------------------------------
# API default: 3001. Web server default: 3000.
# PORT=0 ("let the OS pick a free port") is rejected — an explicit port is
# required. `next dev`/`next start`'s own -p/--port CLI flag, if given,
# overrides this and is what actually gets validated.
PORT=3001

# --- database (api, worker, migration) — SECRET, never expose to web ---
# Must be postgres:// or postgresql://, with either a normal host or a
# host= query parameter (Unix socket form, e.g. Cloud SQL):
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://relis:relis@localhost:5432/relis_control
# DATABASE_URL=postgresql://relis:relis@/relis_control?host=/cloudsql/project:region:instance

# --- web-public (apps/web browser bundle) -------------------------------
# BUILD-TIME value: inlined into the client bundle by `next build` (and on
# every recompile in `next dev`). Changing it after the app is built —
# including at `next start` — does NOT change what's already shipped to
# the browser; you must rebuild. Must be an absolute http(s) URL with a
# real host and no embedded credentials (javascript:, file:, and
# user:pass@host values are all rejected). Never a secret.
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3001

# --- commands that use this file -----------------------------------------
# pnpm dev                 # apps/web/worker/api dev servers (validates first)
# pnpm build                # apps/web build (validates NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL first)
# pnpm check:env -- api     # validate one process without starting it
# pnpm migrate               # validate DATABASE_URL, then run control-DB migrations
# pnpm deploy                # validate everything, then build -> migrate -> start

content.content:
1	# @relis/config
2	
3	Single, typed, Zod-validated environment configuration contract shared by
4	`apps/web`, `apps/api`, `apps/worker`, `packages/database` (migrations),
5	and `tooling` (deployment). Each consumer imports only the loader for its
6	own process, so it never requires or receives configuration it doesn't
7	need.
8	
9	## Variables
10	
11	| Variable | Category | Secret | Required by | Validation |
12	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
13	| `NODE_ENV` | `core` | no | api, worker, web (server) | one of `development`, `test`, `production`; defaults to `development` |
14	| `PORT` | `network` | no | api (default `3001`), web server (default `3000`) | digits only, coerced to an integer in `1..65535`. `PORT=0` ("let the OS pick a free port") is intentionally rejected — the contract requires an explicit port. |
15	| `DATABASE_URL` | `database` | **yes** | api, worker, migration | structurally validated with the WHATWG `URL` parser (not a prefix regex): scheme must be `postgres:` or `postgresql:`, and there must be a host — either a normal network host, or a Unix-socket `?host=/path` query parameter (Prisma's documented form for that case). An out-of-range port (e.g. `:99999`) or an empty host (e.g. `postgresql://user:pass@`) is rejected. |
16	| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `web-public` | no | web (browser) | absolute **http(s)** URL with a real host and **no embedded credentials**; inlined into the client bundle by Next.js at build time. `javascript:`, `file:`, and `user:pass@host` URLs are rejected. |
17	
18	Every variable is declared once in `src/variables.ts`, including its
19	category and secrecy flag; process schemas in `src/processes/*.ts` compose
20	the subset each process actually needs.
21	
22	## Process-specific contracts
23	
24	| Process | Schema | Notes |
25	| --- | --- | --- |
26	| `api` | `apiSchema` (`src/processes/api.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT` + `DATABASE_URL`. |
27	| `worker` | `workerSchema` (`src/processes/worker.ts`) | `NODE_ENV` + `DATABASE_URL`. No `PORT` — the worker has no HTTP surface. No queue/broker variable yet: `background_jobs` is still `undecided` (pg-boss vs. BullMQ) in `stack.yml`. |
28	| `web` (browser) | `webPublicSchema` (`src/processes/web.ts`) | Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`. Never includes `DATABASE_URL` or any other secret. Import via `@relis/config/web-public`, not `@relis/config`. |
29	| `web` (server) | `webServerSchema` | `NODE_ENV` + `PORT`. Still no secrets — the Next.js server in this repository does not talk to the database directly. |
30	| `migration` | `migrationSchema` (`src/processes/migration.ts`) | `DATABASE_URL` only. Called for real by `packages/database`'s `pnpm run migrate` — see that package's README. |
31	
32	`loadAllConfigs()` (`src/load-all.ts`) validates every process above
33	against the same environment and aggregates every failing variable across
34	every process into one `ConfigValidationError` (`process: "deploy"`),
35	instead of stopping at the first failure — used by the deployment gate in
36	`tooling/scripts/deploy.ts`, which needs to report everything wrong before
37	doing anything.
38	
39	## Build-time vs. runtime configuration (apps/web)
40	
41	`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` and `PORT`/`NODE_ENV` are validated at **different
42	times**, because they matter at different times:
43	
44	- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` is a build-time value.** Next.js inlines it
45	  literally into the compiled client JavaScript when you run `next build`
46	  (or on every recompile in `next dev`). Once built, that value is baked
47	  into the shipped bundle — changing the environment variable afterward,
48	  including at `next start` time, does **not** change what's already in
49	  the browser's JavaScript. So `apps/web/scripts/preflight.ts` validates it
50	  at `build` and at `dev`, but deliberately **not** at `start`.
51	- **`PORT`/`NODE_ENV` are runtime values.** They matter only to the
52	  running Next.js server process, so they're validated at `dev` and
53	  `start` (whenever a listener is about to open), not at `build`.
54	
55	This distinction is enforced by `apps/web/scripts/preflight.ts` — see that
56	file and `relis/README.md` for how it gates `next dev`/`next build`/`next
57	start`, including why validating from inside the Next.js process
58	(`apps/web/src/instrumentation.ts`) alone is not sufficient (`PORT=0`
59	gets silently rewritten by Next before an in-process check can see the
60	original value).
61	
62	## Usage
63	
64	```ts
65	// apps/api/src/main.ts
66	import { loadApiConfig, ConfigValidationError } from "@relis/config";
67	
68	try {
69	  const config = loadApiConfig(); // reads process.env
70	  // ... start the server with config.PORT / config.DATABASE_URL
71	} catch (error) {
72	  if (error instanceof ConfigValidationError) {
73	    console.error(JSON.stringify(error.toSafeDiagnostics()));
74	    process.exit(1);
75	  }
76	  throw error;
77	}
78	```
79	
80	```ts
81	// a client component in apps/web
82	import { loadWebPublicConfig } from "@relis/config/web-public";
83	
84	const { NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL } = loadWebPublicConfig();
85	```
86	
87	Note: `loadWebPublicConfig()`'s default argument reads
88	`process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` as a **static member expression** — that
89	exact pattern is what Next.js's compiler recognizes and replaces with a
90	literal value for the client bundle. Don't refactor a caller to pass the
91	whole `process.env` object (or destructure it) instead of calling
92	`loadWebPublicConfig()` bare — that pattern is not something Next.js can
93	statically inline, and `process.env` isn't even defined in the browser at
94	runtime. `apps/web/src/shared/lib/public-config.build.test.ts` is a real
95	`next build` + bundle-content assertion (not just a schema-parsing test)
96	that guards against this regressing silently.
97	
98	## Errors and diagnostics
99	
100	A failed `load*Config()` call throws `ConfigValidationError`. Its `message`,
101	`issues`, and `toSafeDiagnostics()` only ever contain:
102	
103	- the **variable name** (e.g. `DATABASE_URL`),
104	- its **category** (`core` | `network` | `database` | `web-public`), and
105	- a **stable code**: `CONFIG_MISSING` or `CONFIG_INVALID`.
106	
107	The raw value is never read into any of these — safe to log or return from
108	an HTTP diagnostics endpoint as-is. This is verified against real rejected
109	values (including ones containing credentials) in `src/primitives.test.ts`
110	and `src/load-all.test.ts`, not just asserted in a comment.
111	
112	## Deployment / CI validation
113	
114	`src/cli.ts` is a standalone validation entry point:
115	
116	```sh
117	pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- api
118	pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- worker
119	pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- web-public
120	pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- web-server
121	pnpm --filter @relis/config check:env -- migration
122	# from the repo root:
123	pnpm check:env -- api
124	```
125	
126	Exits `0` with `{"status":"valid"}` or `1` with safe diagnostics. Targets
127	are looked up in a `Map`, not a plain object, so a prototype-derived name
128	(`toString`, `constructor`, `__proto__`, `hasOwnProperty`, ...) cannot be
129	silently "found" and treated as a validated process — it's rejected the
130	same as any other unknown target (see `src/cli.test.ts`).
131	
132	This CLI alone is **not** the deployment integration for this repository —
133	it's a building block. The actual gate that gates build/migrate/start
134	behind validation is `tooling/scripts/deploy.ts`; see `relis/README.md`
135	and `tooling/README.md`.
136	
137	## Example values
138	
139	See `relis/.env.example` at the workspace root for safe, non-real sample
140	values for every variable above.
141
